rows.explainer: Mahmud and Riley, “We’re All in This Together”: Addressing Poverty in Village Economics [Presentation - slide 19], April 2024 (unpublished) Note that all numbers reported in Mahmud and Riley are in PPP USD 2023, which is not the units for cost. However, given that we are using PPP USD 2023 values to calculate the log change in consumption, the actual currency units don't matter because we are looking at a proportional change. As long as we use PPP USD 2023 consistently throughout the benefits section, we will get the same units of value regardless of the currency.

Internal validity (unpublished results of a single study) (Best Guess)
rows.explainer: Assumption The key results from Mahmud and Riley that we use in our BOTEC are not yet published and have not yet been peer reviewed, and we do not draw on any other sources of evidence regarding the effectiveness of this program in this BOTEC. The lack of external scrutiny of these results gives us reason to be cautious in our interpretation of them. We may revisit this internal validity adjustment as Muhmud and Riley's paper moves through the peer review process.

rows.label: External validity (Best Guess)
rows.explainer: Assumption It is plausible that these effects won't generalize as RTV expands in Uganda or to other countries. For example, they expanded into new districts for this RCT and it is very plausible that they spent additional resources to ensure that implementation was higher quality in the study villages, and thus that the effects at scale would be lower than Mahmud and Riley's documented effects.

rows.label: Development effects co-benefits (Best Guess)
rows.explainer: Assumption Mahmud and Riley, “We’re All in This Together”: Addressing Poverty in Village Economics [Presentation - slide 55], April 2024 (unpublished) claim that children in households exposed to the RTV program are 4 pp less likely to fall sick and attend 0.4 more days of school each month, which we would reason increases the benefits of the RTV program. Also, if children are consuming dramatically more food for a long period of time, as suggested by the consumption results, this also likely has development effects.

Risk that we learn this is above/below our bar and are wrong
rows.explainer: This captures the possibility that we: i) draw a noisy/biased treatment effect from the trial; ii) update our funding decisions according to the trial; iii) make the wrong ex post decision as a result.

rows.label: Risk that study is funded without us in a few years
rows.explainer: We think other funders might fund the follow-up survey, but are less likely to fund a replication RCT, based on conversations we have had. It is possible that interest in funding a replication RCT could increase once the Mahumd and Riley study results are made public.

Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
